chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the joint hearing of the Committees on Aging, Disabilities, and Finance, and reminds everyone to silence phones and not approach the dais.
chapters.title: Housekeeping and hearing opening

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to the Committee on Aging, jointly with the Committee on Disabilities and the Committee on Finance.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Please place your phone on silent or vibrate mode.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Anytime during the hearing, do not approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, we are ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Council Member Susan Zhuang introduces the oversight hearing on SCRIE and DRIE, thanks co-chairs Lee and Hanif, and summarizes bills including Intro 1011 on eviction disclosures, the pre-considered informational toolkit bill, Resolution 55A on automatic enrollment, Resolution 512 on benefit continuation, and Resolution 610A on full SCHE exemption.
chapters.title: Chair Zhuang opens hearing and outlines bills on agenda

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Susan Zhuang, Chair of the New York City Council's Committee on Aging.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I want to thank you all for being here today for this important oversight hearing on senior citizen rent increase exemption, we call SCRI, and the disability rent increase exemption, DRI.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I also want to say thank you to my co-chairs, Council Member Shahana-K.-Hanif of the Committee on Disability and Council Member Linda-Lee of the

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Committee on Finance for holding this hearing joint with Committee on Aging.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We are also hearing several bills, including a number in the committee.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Including a number in the Committee on Aging, in charge of 1011, sponsored by Councilmember Mealy, could require owner to disclose information to city before evicting older adult's tenant.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: That information could include the name, address, and the phone number of the older adult's occupant.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: It could also require HPD to provide information to those tenants about available legal assistance.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Pre-considered intro number T2026-2546, also sponsored by Council Member

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: toolkit about programs, benefits, and the services available to older adults.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Proposed Resolution 55A, sponsored by Councilmember Caban, calls on New York State legislation to pass and the governor to sign S.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: 2220A-5232, which would allow municipalities and localities

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: localities that have a senior citizen rent increase exemption program to establish an automatic

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: enrollment program for eligible seniors to be automatically enrolled or automatically re-enrolled in the program.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Resolution 512, which I have sponsored, could call upon New York State to pass and the government to sign as

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: 4252-810721 to provide for continuation of senior citizen rent increase exemption or disability rent increase exemption benefits.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: After a peer of ineligibility due to a head of a household

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: called temporary increase in income.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And finally, proposed resolution 610A, which I also

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: sponsored, could call on New York State legislature to pass and the government to sign legislation authorized the city of New York to provide the full exemption

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: from real estate exemption taxation to homeowner eligibility for the senior citizen homeowner exemption.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And those household only source of income is social security.

chapters.summary: Zhuang highlights DFTA's 2025 needs assessment finding one in four older adults lack stable housing, discusses rent burden on fixed incomes, and explains how SCRIE protects seniors from rent increases while providing property tax benefits to owners.
chapters.title: Chair Zhuang on affordability crisis facing older New Yorkers

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Affordability is an issue that so many vulnerable New Yorkers are struggling with.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And it often can make the difference between whether people are able to remain in this city or not.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This is especially true for older New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: A, 2025, DFTA needs assessment of older adults found that one of four older adults

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: survey response, they lack of stable housing, either because they fear of losing their housing in the future or because they current lack of housing.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Older adults are often rent burdened, means that they spend more than 30% of their income on housing while living on fixed income.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This is why programs such as

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Scree are

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: critical to assure eligible older adults are not overburdened by raising rents.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: For so many older adults living on fixed income, even the slightest rent increase can

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: represent the difference between being able to afford basic needs like rent, food, medicine, and transportation or not.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: SCRI is intended to protect seniors from such rent increase, also ensures that property owners receive the

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: corresponding property tax benefits.

chapters.summary: Zhuang notes many eligible older New Yorkers are unaware of SCRIE, cites burdensome documentation requirements and income eligibility ceilings as drivers of under-enrollment, and outlines goals for understanding agency outreach across cultural, linguistic, and disability communities.
chapters.title: Chair Zhuang on SCRIE awareness gaps and enrollment barriers

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: While programs like SCRI exist, they are only effective if people know about them.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Many eligible older New Yorkers are unaware of this program.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This city needs to do better at assuring everyone has access

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: to the benefit that they are entitled to.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Beyond awareness, this program also run more efficiently and impactfully if specific changes were made to improve the program.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: There are many barriers to

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: enroll and utilize of those programs.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: For example, providing certain documents in order to complete application for SCRI can be overly burdensome.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And the income eligibility ceiling in the rent freeze program also central

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: driver of under in arrangement in the program.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Today we want to have a better understanding of how the New York City Department of Aging, NYC Department of Finance, NYC Aging and the Department of Housing Prevention and Development

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: preservation and development and the mayor's office of people with disabilities conduct research to ensure seniors across all culture, ethnic backgrounds, those who live with disabilities,

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: those who are limited English proficiency, and those who may not have access to internet gain information about screen and the dream.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We also want to understand how the city is using the data we have at our disposal to ensure those who are eligible for those benefits are actually enrolled in them.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This is our understanding that programs are underutilized.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We must work to change that.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We also want to call on our state counterpart to make changes to screen the dream to ensure more property owners to participate in this program.

chapters.summary: Zhuang presents Resolution 431 on property tax incentives for senior housing, Resolution 470 on expanding DRIE household eligibility, and Resolution 471 on shifting SCHE income verification to state tax department, then thanks committee staff and recognizes attending colleagues.

utterances.text: And to encourage a system more order adults in enrolling.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Among the many pieces of legislation, our community is

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Our hearing today, I also sponsor legislation that focuses on those goals.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Resolution 431 calls upon New York State legislature to pass and the government to sign legislation to authorize property tax intensive for property owner who dedicate 20%

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: of existing housing stock to senior citizens and individuals experiencing homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And finally, Resolution No.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: S-4805-A4984, which could shift the income verification responsibility for the senior citizen homeowner exemption from local governments to the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you to my colleagues for joining me today to NYC Aging and all the other agencies for Testify and to my staff, Jennifer, Sorm Moscon, committee staff.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Anita Kilawa.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Joshua Newman.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Julia Hamas.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Julia Hermes, Margaret Bursley, Kobe Porter, Amy Josco, and Brooke Fry.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Before we continue, I want to recognize my colleagues who are here with us today.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We have Councilmember Marte, Dinerwoods, Marmarong, Brewer, Schumann, Hudson, Epstein, Cabon, Wong, Lewis, Mercedes, Narcisse,

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Sanchez, Banks, Brooks-Power.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We have on the Zoom, Joseph, Abreu, and I think also Abdul.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Now I give the floor to my co-chair, Councilmember Lee, for her to give a statement.

chapters.summary: Council Member Linda Lee outlines Finance Committee bills including Intro 307 on universal SCRIE/DRIE applications, Intro 934 on SCHE income categories, Intro 978A on income limit increases, Intro 1010 on SCHE/DHE thresholds, Intro 1033 on notice requirements, and the pre-considered training bill, then discusses the importance of rent freeze programs for older adults and people with disabilities.
chapters.title: Chair Lee on Finance Committee bills and hearing purpose

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you so much, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: It's so great to see all the folks from the admin, as well as all of our amazing advocates who are joining us today.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: My name is Linda Lee, Chair of the Committee on Finance, and I'd also like to thank my colleagues, Councilmember Susan Zhuang and Councilmember Shahana Hanif, who are both co-chairing this hearing with me.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And we're also hearing several bills today, which will be included in the Committee on Finance, so bear with me while I read these.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Intro 307, sponsored by Councilmember Marte, would establish a universal application and recertification system for the Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption Program and Disability Rent Increase Exemption Program.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Intro 934, sponsored by Councilmember Simcha-Felder, would require the creation of additional annual income categories and corresponding exemption percentages for certain households eligible for the senior citizens'homeowners'exemption.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Proposed Intro 978A, sponsored by Councilmember Farah-Lewis, would require the city to increase the maximum income level qualifying for exemption from rent increases granted to certain senior citizens and persons with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Intro 1010, sponsored by Councilmember Christopher-Marte, would increase the maximum income level qualifying for the senior citizen homeowners exemption and the disabled homeowners exemption.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Intro 1030.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: sponsored by Simca Felder, would make certain informational requirements for notices concerning rent increase exemption programs discretionary.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: A pre-considered bill sponsored by Councilmember Christopher Banks would require the dissemination of information on the rent freeze program and training for participating agencies.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Resolution 431, sponsored by Councilmember Susan Zhuang, calls on New York State legislature

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: to pass and the governor to sign legislation authorizing property tax incentives for property owners who dedicate 20% of existing housing stock to senior citizens and individuals experiencing homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Resolution 470, sponsored by Councilmember Susan Zhuang, calls on New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign S3563 and A10927

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: to permit other qualifying members of a household to qualify for the Disability Rent Increase Exemption.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And finally, Resolution No.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: 471 calls on the New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign S4805.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Slash A4984, which would shift income verification responsibilities for the senior citizen homeowners exemption from local governments to the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance.

chapters.summary: Lee emphasizes the need to identify persistent barriers to program access, references public charge concerns, and thanks Finance Committee staff and ASL interpreters before passing the microphone to Chair Hanif.
chapters.title: Chair Lee on agency collaboration and staff acknowledgments

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: This hearing and the proposed legislation are intended to ensure that no New Yorker living with a disability and no older adult on a limited

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: fixed income has to choose between paying rent and paying for daily necessities such as food, medicine, heat, cooling, or electricity.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: The rent freeze programs administered here in New York City by HPD and DOF provide the much needed relief that allows for a vibrant older adult and disabilities communities to contribute and exist without facing cost barriers to do so.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: During my time as president and CEO of a nonprofit providing services to the very communities at the center of today's hearing, this was and remains a prevalent issue.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Communities faced and continue to face cultural language barriers to understanding, accessing, and making full use of the programs designed to provide them relief.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And one example is that we saw this during public charge several years ago.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: It is my hope that today's hearing helps us identify where those barriers persist and what more can be done to close them.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And as Chair Wang mentioned, I'm excited that we are able to convene the agencies and offices of DOF, New York City Aging, HPD, and MOPD

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: to understand how we can maximize collaboration on our end to ensure the success of these programs and to ensure that New Yorkers can fully take advantage of them and are provided adequate support and materials to do so.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you to my colleagues for joining me today, to DOF and all other agencies for testifying, and to the Finance Committee staff, Julia Jaramis, Owen Katowski, Margaret Barnsley, Aman Mahadevan, and Valeria Lazaro-Rodriguez.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Also want to give a special thanks to the

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Give us.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Special shout out to our ASL interpreters who are helping out today for our disabilities community.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So let's give them a round, or sorry, raise of hands applause.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And now I hand it back over to my co-chair, Councilmember Shwayne.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Now I pass the microphone to Councilor, Councilor, Councilmember Hanif for her to give a statement.

chapters.summary: Council Member Shahana Hanif describes the DRIE program's purpose, notes nearly one in six New Yorkers has a disability, and explains how DRIE freezes rent for low-income tenants with disabilities through property tax credits to owners.
chapters.title: Chair Hanif on DRIE program and disability housing crisis

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Swang, and good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Shahana Hanif, Chair of the Committee on Disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: I'm a brown woman in my mid-30s, though I do look younger.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Today I'm wearing...

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Today I'm wearing a full sleeve black coat.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: I'm not wearing glasses, which I usually wear.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: I'm in my contacts and I'm seated behind a dais next to my colleagues, council members.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: All right, colleagues, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Everybody's just looking at me.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Everybody's making fun of me right now.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you for inviting the Disabilities Committee to join this important hearing where we will discuss the Disability Rent Increase Exemption, or DRI, program in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Nearly one in six New Yorkers lives with a disability, and New Yorkers with disabilities are far more likely to have lower income, to rent rather than own, and to be severely rent burdened.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: For someone living on a fixed...

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: disability benefit, a rent increase is not an inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: It can be the difference between staying housed and not.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: The DREAM program exists to stop that from happening.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: It freezes rent for a low-income tenant with a disability and reimburses the owner through a property tax credit.

chapters.summary: Hanif details DRIE enrollment falling from 12,215 households in 2019 to 11,012 in 2024, notes 42% enrollment among eligible households down from 56%, and highlights the Bronx as the only borough with declining DRIE enrollment, with Morrisania and East Tremont having under 25% enrollment.
chapters.title: Chair Hanif on DRIE enrollment decline and borough disparities

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Yet the program is not reaching the people it was built for.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: DRE enrollment peaked at 12,215 households in 2019.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: By 2024, it was 11,012, a decline of nearly 10%, while the cost of housing in New York City went in exactly the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Across both SCRI and DRE, the Department of Finance estimates that roughly 158,000 households were eligible in 2023.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: And that roughly 42% of them were enrolled, down from 56% four years earlier.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: The Bronx is the only borough where DRE enrollment fell, and the Bronx neighborhoods report some of the lowest rent-freeze program utilization rates in our city.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: In Morissania and East Tremont, fewer than a quarter of eligible households are enrolled in either SCRI or DRE.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: That is not a coincidence.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: It shows us where outreach is not working.

chapters.summary: Hanif reports the median DRIE recipient household income is $16,671 with tenants paying 62% of income toward frozen rent, and 16% have frozen rent exceeding their entire household income, arguing freezing rent at unaffordable levels defeats the program's purpose.
chapters.title: Chair Hanif on affordability gaps for enrolled DRIE recipients

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: But enrollment is only half the problem.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Among DRI recipients in 2024, the median household income was $16,671.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: And the median tenant was paying 62% of their income toward frozen rent.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: 16% had a frozen rent that exceeded their entire reported household income.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: These are households the city already enrolled and counted as a success.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: And they're still paying rents they cannot afford.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Freezing rent at an unaffordable number is not the point of the program.

chapters.summary: Hanif acknowledges DOF's SCRIE/DRIE ombudspersons, PEU's rent freeze outreach, and MOPD's housing access documentation, then shares a constituent case involving months-long SCRIE renewal delays that nearly depleted a senior's Social Security.
chapters.title: Chair Hanif on city outreach steps and constituent case

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: It's important to note that the city has taken real steps, and the agencies in this room deserve recognition for them.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: The Department of Finance has maintained the office of the SCRI and DRI ombudspersons.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: The Public Engagement Unit's Rent Freeze team has done direct outreach to tenants who failed to renew.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: The Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities continues to document housing access barriers in accessible NYC, and this work absolutely matters.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: I have seen the programmatic impacts and gaps up close.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Just this past summer, a constituent's daughter reached out to support her parent on a SCRI renewal, facing an extended delay of months on end and resulting in full rent being charged.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: My constituents'social security was renewed.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: nearly depleted, and she had little money for basic necessities.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Our office was fortunately able to connect them to the public engagement unit's rent-free office and resolve the issue.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: But there are countless stories like this out there, and we have to do better.

chapters.summary: Hanif emphasizes DRIE is not an older adult program with eligibility starting at 18 and average recipient age of 64, notes working-age disabled tenants won't see themselves in senior-focused outreach, and asks about targeted outreach before thanking staff and colleagues.
chapters.title: Chair Hanif on DRIE age demographics and outreach gaps

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: To return to DRI, I want to make clear that this is not an older adult program.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Eligibility starts at 18, and the average DRI householder is 64 years old, 13 years younger than the average SCRI recipient.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: A working-age tenant with a disability is unlikely to see themselves in outreach built around older adult centers and mailings to seniors.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: When a benefit is bundled under a heading that doesn't describe you, you don't apply for it.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Today, I want to hear from the Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities and the Department of Finance about how outreach efforts attempt to reach that New Yorker specifically.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you to the administration for being here today and to the disability advocates, tenant organizers, legal service providers.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: And members of the public who have traveled to testify or submitted written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Your presence here is an act of self-advocacy, and we do not take it for granted.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you to all of the staff who have made today's hearing possible, including the Disabilities Committee staff, Senior Legislative Counsel Sarah Sucher, and Senior Legislative Policy Analyst Chloe Rivera.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: And Emmett Teran, my legislative director and senior advisor.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: And Simone Lavin, my communications director.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: I would also like to recognize that we've been joined by Councilmember Ressler, and I will now pass the mic back to Chair Zhuang.

utterances.speaker: Shahana Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I will now pass the mic to Councilmember Marte to give a statement on his legislation.

chapters.summary: Council Member Christopher Marte thanks committee chairs and advocates, describes the programs as critical anti-displacement tools, and explains Intro 1010 which implements the state's increased income eligibility to $75,000 for SCHE and DHE, giving tens of thousands more seniors and disabled homeowners access to tax breaks.
chapters.title: CM Marte on SCRIE/DRIE/SCHE/DHE importance and Intro 1010

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: My name is Councilmember Christopher Marte.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: I'm a brown male wearing a blue suit, white shirt, and a red tie with little camels on it.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: I like to say you look younger than your age.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: I look maybe younger than my age, but.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: I would like to thank our committee chairs today, Councilmember Lee, Councilmember Hanif, Councilmember Zhang for today's important hearing.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Thank you to the committee staff who has been helping us with these bills and organizing this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: And lastly, I want to thank all the advocates that are here today.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: SCREED, DRE, SHE, and DE are some of the most important programs to stop displacement, address our city's urgent affordability crisis, and keep people in their homes.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: The skyrocketing cost of living compounded with the astronomical rent increases means that more and more New Yorkers are finding themselves just scraping by.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Seniors and people with disability, people on fixed incomes, are the most vulnerable to rising costs.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: For too long, the eligibility criteria for these programs have not reflected the economic realities of many New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: workers now face and our hands have been tied.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Thankfully, the state has allowed us to raise the maximum income eligibility to $75,000.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Intro 1010 will implement this change for she and he, giving tens of thousands more seniors and people

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: disabled homeowners access to these tax breaks.

chapters.summary: Marte details how Mitchell-Lama tenants must use HPD's paper-only SCRIE process while other tenants use DOF's online system, causing confusion and delays, and explains Intro 307 would create a single universal online application and recertification portal regardless of agency.
chapters.title: CM Marte on Intro 307 universal SCRIE application portal

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Along with Councilmember Lewis, Intro 978, we must pass these bills immediately to increase housing affordability for renters and homeowners alike.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: We are also hearing my bill, Intro 307, which will require a universal online

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: SCRI application portal.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: While most of SCRI is handled by Department of Finance, Mitchell Lama tenants receive SCRI through HPD.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Despite the fact that it's exact same benefits, the process is different for each agency.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: The DOF has a user-friendly website that makes it easy to apply, recertify, and stay on top of your SCRI application while also having a paper option.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: HPD, on the other hand, only has a different paper application that you can mail in or email to a general inbox or even sometimes fax.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Yes, we're talking about faxing documents in 2026.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: For many seniors,

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: tenants in Michilama, this can be incredibly confusing.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: People accidentally submit DOF applications to each HPD, not realizing they are different.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: My

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: My office has had constituents who had applied to SCRI multiple times because they mailed in their application to HPD and waited months only to find out that HPD had no record of their application.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: This system of two different processes for the same benefits only leads to delay and confusion.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Intro 307 will simplify this process requiring a single online application for recertification portal for SCRI regardless of which agency you're applying from.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: This easy fix will make SCRI more accessible to Mitchell Almatonets all over New York City.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: I look forward to today's hearing and urge my colleagues to support these bills so we can quickly pass them.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And thank you, Councilmember Marte.

chapters.summary: Council Member Tiffany Cabán notes over 1.5 million seniors live in the city with many on fixed incomes, shares her experience as a law student helping with SCRIE/DRIE applications, and urges passage of Resolution 55 calling on the state to authorize automatic enrollment for eligible seniors.
chapters.title: CM Cabán on Resolution 55 for automatic SCRIE enrollment

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I will pass the microphone to Councilmember Caban to give a statement on her legislation.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: My name is Councilmember Tiffany Caban.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: I am a 39-year-old Latina female wearing a gray suit, glasses, and my signature ponytail.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: I will keep it very brief so we can get this show on the road.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: There are over 1.5 million seniors living in our city.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: That's half a million more than we had in 2006, and many of them are living on fixed incomes as the cost of living here continues to soar amidst this historic affordability crisis.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: And when rent and maintenance costs go up, too many senior citizens are forced to choose between housing, food, and medicine.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: And the senior citizen rent increase exemption, or SCRI, can be life-saving by covering the cost of rent and maintenance increases for seniors struggling to get by.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: I see it now.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: My colleagues see it now when our constituents come into our offices.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: And this has been a persistent problem.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: You know, I saw it as a law student.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: One of my very first legal internships, I worked at Lenox Hill Neighborhood House supporting seniors and people with disabilities with their SCRI and DRE applications.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: And the challenges existed then, but they're exacerbated now.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: Too many seniors don't know about SCRI or struggle to re-enroll year after year, and there's no reason for us to place this bureaucratic burden on senior citizens when enrollment could be automatic.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: So that's why we're hearing this resolution today, and thank you that that's happening.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: And the resolution calls on our friends at the state level to pass and implement.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: Senate Bill 2220, Assembly Bill 5232, so that our city can automatically enroll our senior citizens in this life-saving program.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Now let me pass the mic to Councilmember Banks.

chapters.summary: Council Member Chris Banks explains his pre-considered bill requiring DOF to provide annual SCRIE/DRIE training to designated personnel at city agencies serving older adults and people with disabilities, covering eligibility, applications, renewals, accommodations, and referrals, with annual reporting to the Council.
chapters.title: CM Banks on agency training and rent freeze outreach bill

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairs, and thank you to my colleagues for the opportunity to speak on this important legislation.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: For many older adults here in New Yorkers with disabilities, a scree injury can mean the difference between remaining in their homes and being displaced by another rent increase.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: As we all know, our city is in the midst of an affordability crisis, and these programs are critical.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: But they only work when eligible New Yorkers know they exist and receive accurate guidance when they ask for help.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Too often, residents visit a city agency seeking assistance but leave even more confused without clear information about whether they qualify or how to apply or how to renew

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: their benefits or where to submit an application.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: A misrenewal or an incorrect referral can place someone's housing stability at risk.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And this is, in this affordability crisis, that's something that we can't risk and we can't afford to take.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: This bill addresses that service gap.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: It would require the Department of Finance to provide annual SCRI and DREES training to designated personnel at city agencies that regularly serve older adults and people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: The training would cover eligibility requirements, application renewal procedures, key program features, reasonable accommodations, and proper referrals.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: The bill would also expand existing outreach requirements to include DRE,

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: add the Mayor's Office of People with Disabilities as a participating agency, and require annual reporting to the council so we can ensure that the training is taking place.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: The principle is simple.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: When New Yorkers reach out to their government for help, they should receive accurate information and be directed to the right place.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: They should not be sent from office to office or risk losing benefits because the person assisting them was never properly trained.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Every city agency that regularly services older adults and people with disabilities should be equipped to connect eligible residents with these rent-freeze programs.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: For our constituents, that knowledge can protect their homes, preserves their independence, and provides much-needed financial stability.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: So again, I urge the members of this joint committee and every member of the council to sign.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: and support this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Together, we can make the city government easier to navigate and ensure that screen injury reached New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: These programs were created to protect.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Now I will pass the microphone to Councilmember Lewis to give the statement on her legislation.

chapters.summary: Council Member Farah Louis presents Intro 978A to increase the SCRIE/DRIE income ceiling from $50,000 to $75,000 retroactive to July 1, 2026, citing DOF data showing 67,677 enrolled versus 158,214 eligible households, and noting median rent-to-income ratios of 56% for SCRIE and 62% for DRIE recipients.
chapters.title: CM Louis on Intro 978A raising income threshold to $75,000

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Good morning and thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Farrah Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I'm a black woman wearing a lilac suit and mid-length hair.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I want to thank Chairs Zhuang, Lee, and Hanif for convening today's hearing and for your support to bring Intro 978A before the Council.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I am proud to sponsor Intro 978A, which would amend the Administrative Code to increase the maximum household income for eligibility for senior citizen rent increase exemption,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: also known as SCRI, and disability rent increase exemption, also known as DRI.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: From $50,000 to $75,000 beginning in July 1, 2026, making it retroactive to date.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This legislation is necessary because the need for rent stabilization among our seniors and New Yorkers with disabilities is significant and growing.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: According to the Department of Finance, 67,677 households received SCRI

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: or DRI benefits in 2024, while 158,214 households were potentially eligible in 2023.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That gap demonstrates that thousands of New Yorkers who could potentially benefit from these protections remain outside of the program.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For those who are enrolled, the program provides meaningful relief.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: In 2024, the average monthly SCRI benefit was approximately $200.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: while the average DREE benefit was approximately $261.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: In Brooklyn, the average monthly benefit was $243.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Yet the underlying affordability challenge remains severe.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The 2025 report found that the median rent to income ratio among SCRI recipients was 56%, and among DREE recipients, it was 62%.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: By raising the threshold to $75,000, we can extend this important protection for more New Yorkers and strengthen housing stability for people who have spent decades building their lives and communities here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I look forward to working with my colleagues, the administration, advocates, and our constituents to ensure that this expanded protection reaches every eligible New Yorker who needs it the most.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Since we have ASL interpreter here, we will give the testimony for Mr.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: So first.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Saul?

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Then we'll go to the administration.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Representing the Metropolitan Asian Deaf Association, Clement So describes how deaf seniors face systemic barriers including lack of ASL-accessible eligibility notices, phone-based administrative systems, and tight recertification timelines, and urges mandatory accessible notices, direct ASL video appointments at DOF, and funded community-based navigation support.
chapters.title: Clement So testifies on deaf seniors' barriers to DRIE

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Okay, good morning chairs and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: My name is Clement So, and I am representing the Metropolitan Asian Deaf Association, or MADA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today on housing stability for deaf and hard of hearing senior citizens across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Housing affordability is a critical issue for deaf seniors living on fixed incomes such as SSI or SSDI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: While programs like DRI and SCRI are vital lifelines, deaf seniors face systematic barriers that prevent them from accessing these protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: First, many deaf seniors never receive notice of DRI eligibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: They face sudden rent increases without accessible prior notice, and many remain completely unaware that DRI exists to freeze their rent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Unknowingly, they pay unaffordable increases for years or face severe eviction risks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: This is all due to a lack of knowledge, I mean lack of language access resources available to support them like ASL resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Second, administrative communication is heavily phone-based.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Managing DRI issues or following up on applications rely on systems like 311.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Calling through the video relay service leads to long wait times, dropped calls, and representatives untrained in handling relay calls.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: There are no direct visual channels such as ASL video appointments or direct email ticket support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Third, language barriers and tight timelines create constant hurdles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Complex legal notices are rarely available in American Sign Language or plain language.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: When recertification notices arrive late in the mail, deaf seniors often lose their frozen rent status simply because they lacked accessible support to process the paperwork in time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: We urge the City Council to take these three clear actions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: One, mandate proactive jury notices whenever landlords issue rent increases to tenants receiving disability benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Two, establish direct ASL video appointments and dedicated email support at the Department of Finance so deaf applicants do not have to rely on 311.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Sorry, third, fund community-based organizations to provide targeted, hands-on DRE navigation for deaf and hard-of-hearing New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Clement So
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and commitment to equitable housing access.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: So.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And I committed, our city council definitely will work with you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
