chapters.summary: Dora Carreno, testifying individually, notes that despite SCRIE enacted in 1970 and DRIE in 2005, only 42% of eligible households are enrolled, calling it shameful and urging passage of Intros 978, 307, and Resolution 55, plus comprehensive public messaging from the council, mayor's office, and Office of Mass Engagement.
chapters.title: Dora Carreno testifies on enrollment failures and outreach gaps

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: I just want to point out that although SCRI was enacted in 1970 and DRI in 2005, where we stand right now, we're only at 42% of people who qualify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: Being enrolled in this program and that is absolutely shameful and speaks volumes of the commitment of the state and the city towards those people who need the support the most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: We are failing people abysmally when it comes to keeping people housed and bringing people out of the harm of homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: We need to do better, not just by passing bills and passing resolutions, but once enacting them, making sure that people know that these services are, that these programs are available.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: Many people don't have access to the internet or do not know how to use the internet to be able to do the research and find out that these things are there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: It is the city's job and the state's job to make sure that people know, have the education and the support to be able to fill out these applications and partake in these programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: So I urge you to pass intros 978, 307.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: 0055, as well as urge you to make sure that there's more messaging out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: there from city council, from the mayor's office, the office of mass engagement, all hands should be on deck making sure that we prevent people from losing their homes, especially people who are

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: elderly, low income, disabled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: We just got to do better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dora Carreno
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: And let's go back to Mabaki DM.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Are you ready this time?

chapters.summary: Maka Cham of the Center for Independence of the Disabled New York highlights that over 90,000 eligible households remain unenrolled in SCRIE/DRIE, and strongly supports Intros 934, 978, 1010, 470, 307, and Resolution 55, urging expanded outreach strategies to close the enrollment gap for people with disabilities.
chapters.title: Maka Cham testifies for CIDNY on disability enrollment gaps

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: I apologize about the issues earlier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: My name is Mabaki Chang.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: I'm the housing and health community organizer here at Center for Independence of the Disabled New York Advocate for People with Disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: In the fabric of New York City to live independently.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: So I'm here today, excited to join you and highlight the importance of the three programs for people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: So I will start from, you know, mentioning the need

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: of the expansion of the programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: So three and three are essentials, housing protection for seniors and people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Eligible New Yorkers, age 18 and older can receive three if they meet the income

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: and rent burden requirements and receive qualifying disability benefits such as SSI, SSDI, certain disability-related Medicaid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: or qualifying veterans or federal disability benefit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Just like Scree for eligible New Yorkers age 62 and older.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: DREAM is essential for our consumers as it helps freeze the tenants'rent and provides the landlords with a property tax credit for the exempted increase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: According to 2023 data, NYCDOF estimated that 158,218 households were eligible, but only 67,132 were currently enrolled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: That means that over 90,000 households, which is around 57 to 60 percent, are eligible but not enrolled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: So we need to promote the outreach strategies in order to expand the program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: That is why we strongly support the bills below.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Intro 934, Intro 978, Wisconsin Member Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Intro 1010, Wisconsin Member Martez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Intro 470, Wisconsin Member and Chair Zhuang.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: We also want to work in helping the city to make the program.

utterances.speaker: Speaker
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: So I will just resume and say we also support intro 307 and 308.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: and Resolution 55.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: We look forward to working with the city in improving the screen entry programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: And also may have...

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: Joint hearing of the Committees on Aging, Disabilities, and Finance on SCRIE/DRIE rent freeze programs, covering multiple bills to raise income eligibility from $50,000 to $75,000, create a universal application portal, expand homeowner exemptions, and improve agency outreach and training.

Agency testimony from DOF, DFTA, HPD, and MOPD on enrollment data showing 42% of eligible households enrolled, with extensive Q&A on outreach gaps, language access, Bronx enrollment declines, renewal rates, disability accommodations, and cross-agency coordination challenges.

Public testimony from over 30 advocates, legal service providers, community organizations, and residents overwhelmingly supporting the legislation, plus unscheduled testimony from EMS workers on staffing and pay crises affecting response times for vulnerable New Yorkers.
title: Committee on Aging
topic: Oversight - Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE) and Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE)
